decision_description: Contradiction between two Tier 4 Phase 7 budget artifacts for the FIELDWISE MSCA-PF action: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json declares gate_pass_declaration='fail' (BLK-01: no lump-sum response present in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/), while docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/gate_result.json records gate_09_budget_consistency status='pass' via the deterministic unit-cost derivation captured in unit_cost_budget.json (total EUR 220723.5; every line item, including the host-dependent living_allowance, resolved to Confirmed; no unresolved components). The specific issue is which Tier 4 budget artifact governs the Phase 7 gate for this instrument, and consequently whether the §13.4 concern raised by the compliance validator against the Phase 8 drafting_review_status.json is a genuine blocking violation. The instrument regime is resolved to unit_cost from Tier 3 docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json (MSCA-PF), so the lump-sum-mode budget_gate_assessment.json 'fail' is not applicable and the gate evaluator's gate_result.json is the authoritative gate record. RESOLUTION: the Tier 4 gate_result.json (unit-cost, gate_09 pass) prevails over the Tier 4 lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json (fail); gate_09 was satisfied before Phase 8 commenced.
alternatives_considered: Treat budget_gate_assessment.json (lump-sum, 'fail') as the governing Phase 7 record and declare a §13.4 blocking violation freezing Phase 8 — rejected because MSCA-PF is a unit-cost instrument per Tier 3 call_binding/selected_call.json, for which the lump-sum received/ channel does not apply under §8.1/§8.4 (C1 amendment); the lump-sum assessment is a not-applicable mode artifact.

Surface the contradiction to the human operator as an unresolved conflict per §3 rather than resolving it — unnecessary because the contradiction is resolvable by subordination to the explicit instrument-conditional budget-gate rule (§8.4) and the exclusive gate-evaluation authority (§17.6.2); recorded here as resolved with the prevailing tier and reasoning per §12.3.

Silently defer to the more convenient artifact without a recorded resolution — prohibited by §12.3 and §13.5; every resolved tier conflict must produce a durable decision log entry naming the prevailing authority.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.4 and §8.1 (instrument-conditional budget gate; the deterministic unit-cost derivation is the sole sanctioned budget source for MSCA-PF) resolving the conflict between Tier 4 gate_result.json (gate_09_budget_consistency, unit-cost, pass) and Tier 4 budget_gate_assessment.json (lump-sum, fail); gate-evaluation authority per CLAUDE.md §17.6.2; §12.3 explicit-contradiction-resolution rule; instrument regime taken from Tier 3 call_binding/selected_call.json
rationale: Per the C1 constitutional amendment to §8.1/§8.4, the Phase 7 budget gate is instrument-conditional by source: for unit-cost instruments such as MSCA-PF the budget is produced by the sanctioned internal deterministic derivation (confirmed_months × published_rates × host_country_coefficient), validated by a byte-equal replay check, and NOT by an external lump-sum response in received/. gate_result.json shows gate_09 passed on the unit-cost predicates (g08_uc01, g08_uc02, g08_uc03, g08_p01) with the lump-sum predicates (g08_p02–g08_p09) correctly skipped as not-applicable for the resolved unit_cost regime, and the cross-run provenance quad in phase8_checkpoint.json records gate_09 as legitimately inherited from the unit-cost derivation run 49dc10ca. Gate evaluation is exclusively the scheduler/gate-evaluator's authority (§17.6.2); the lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json 'fail' reflects a Mode-B validation path that does not apply to this instrument and cannot override a passed gate_09. Because gate_09 passed, the categorical and instrument-independent §8.4 Phase-8 block was satisfied before Phase 8 drafting/review began, so the §13.4 concern is not a genuine blocking violation. Choosing the lump-sum 'fail' artifact as governing would resolve the contradiction by selecting the incorrect/more convenient source, which §12.3 expressly prohibits; the correct resolution is to name the prevailing tier authority (§8.4 unit-cost derivation, authoritative gate_result.json) and record it durably.
